Why It Matters To Us: A generic datapack condition keyed on a registry id or tag reaches this mod's content with no dependency and no code. The condition is simply never satisfied when the mod is absent.
What We Actually Do: Nothing. Write the title JSON.
Notes: This is the overwhelming majority of integration and it is why the datapack vocabulary matters more than any Java compat class

Why It Matters To Us: The pack author drives us. Their quest or script calls our command as a reward.
What We Actually Do: Keep the command surface clean and scriptable
Notes: Zero code on either side. Probably our single highest-value integration path

Why It Matters To Us: We want to read or write something only this mod defines.
What We Actually Do: One isolated class behind a ModList.get().isLoaded() guard - never referenced from a field type in a loaded class
Notes: Per the Integration dependencies decision. Core must load and play correctly with it absent

Why It Matters To Us: Grants attributes of its own. Does not need code from us - it needs our additive-only rule to be correct.
What We Actually Do: Nothing. Listed so we remember why the Stacking with other mods rule exists
Notes: See the Balance Model sheet

Why It Matters To Us: Alters the damage or attribute pipeline in a way that could make our numbers behave differently than we expect.
What We Actually Do: Test in-game before trusting any balance number
Notes: Cannot be resolved on paper

Why It Matters To Us: Registers 21 real attributes on 1.20.1 - crit_chance - crit_damage - life_steal - overheal - ghost_health - armor_pierce - armor_shred - prot_pierce - prot_shred - dodge_chance - draw_speed - arrow_damage - arrow_velocity - current_hp_damage - fire_damage - cold_damage - healing_received - mining_speed - experience_gained - elytra_flight - creative_flight
What We Actually Do: One compat class letting title effects target attributeslib attributes when it is loaded. Skip the effect silently when it is not.
Notes: THE most valuable single integration - present in both packs we have data for. mining_speed and experience_gained also map onto effects the Effect Catalog currently has to implement with event hooks. Namespace is attributeslib NOT apothic_attributes - verified against ALObjects.java on the 1.20 branch

Why It Matters To Us: Raises or removes the hard-coded min and max bounds vanilla puts on attributes. Its presence is direct evidence that this pack expects inflated attribute totals.
What We Actually Do: Nothing - but config validation must not accept a cap value that vanilla would silently clamp when AttributeFix is absent
Notes: The clearest single proof that clamping the player's final attribute value would have been the wrong design

Why It Matters To Us: Grants attributes directly through a skill tree. Stacks with everything else.

Why It Matters To Us: Levelling system granting attribute points as the player levels

Mod or Group: CONCLUSION - what to build for pack authors
Why It Matters To Us: Ship example title JSON for Cataclysm and Mowzies since they appear in all three packs - and document the condition vocabulary properly
